title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing distinction and documented governance controls are supported. One checklist instruction asks administrators to review write tools without a corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans federated connectors for governed Work IQ access to additional enterprise data sources.
claims.quote: Enable Work IQ to use federated connectors for governed access to additional enterprise data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Microsoft Graph and Work IQ as products.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Graph", "Work IQ"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the cloud listed in the roadmap.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: Developer is the platform listed in the roadmap.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Developer"]

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this Work IQ federated-connectors capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors default enable participation admin control MCP policy API policy settings; Work IQ federated connectors enable default. Read roadmap, Work IQ overview and federated connector overviews; connector defaults do not state this capability's arrival default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors use Model Context Protocol to fetch external data in real time.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity and schema tools.
claims.quote: Connected enterprise sources participate in Work IQ Copilot, entity, and schema tools. Connected enterprise sources refer to data sources connected in Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Connector developers must enable participation in Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Live external data is retrieved into Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Copilot selects relevant connector tools at runtime and uses the live results returned by the source to respond in the conversation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector provides tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.

claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in the Researcher agent.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.claim: The general connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, unlike the specific overview's write-action documentation.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: MCP server firewalls may need static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Users querying federated Copilot sources need a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence or Microsoft 365 E7.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses consumption billing through Copilot Credits, supporting the consumption licensing model and variable cost rating.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Foundry page distinguishes usage-billed A2A, REST and MCP Work IQ API access from connector-backed tools' connector-specific licensing.
claims.quote:
Work IQ API through A2A, REST, or MCP | Usage-based billing ... This path doesn't use connector licensing.
Connector-backed Microsoft 365 tools | Connector licensing | Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites.

claims.claim: Connector enable, disable and staging controls are reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector.
claims.quote:
Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration.
Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The block and unblock Package Management APIs require a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Block and unblock require delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available.
Application | Not available. | Not available.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support these beta APIs in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The block and unblock operations do not configure staged rollout.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
Request body
Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: No automation for federated connector staged rollout is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connector staged rollout Microsoft Graph API automation. Read custom federated connector setup, manage federated connectors and Package Management API overview; results document connector staging in the admin center, not an automation operation for that setting.

claims.claim: The custom federated connector documentation says Block has the same effect as Disable.
claims.quote: Block (Agents > Tools) | Same as Disable.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock allows use of a blocked package.
claims.quote:
Unblock a Copilot package to allow its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 admin-center allow and block controls for Copilot Connectors also apply through Work IQ APIs.
claims.quote: Existing administrator controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center to allow or block Copilot Connectors also apply when Connectors are accessed through Work IQ APIs.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access controls connector availability by publisher type.
claims.quote: Turn off connectors in bulk by publisher type in Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access, then turn on specific connectors from Your connections.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with mode applyOnce can set publisher-type access.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue.

claims.claim: Publisher access uses resourceType microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes with valueObject properties areMicrosoftAppsAllowed, areTenantScopedAppsAllowed and areISVAppsAllowed.
claims.quote:
"resourceType": "microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes",
"resourceVersion": 1,
"properties": {
  "valueObject": {
    "areMicrosoftAppsAllowed": true,
    "areTenantScopedAppsAllowed": true,
    "areISVAppsAllowed": false,

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls which users may use connectors.
claims.quote:
Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts.
Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors with mode applyOnce can set User access.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.

claims.claim: microsoft.agent.useraccess sets valueObject.userAssignmentCategory to everyone or noOne, without specific-group assignment in the documented schema.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: Creating an applyOnce monitor requires the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads

claims.claim: Agent-resource applyOnce needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite on the TCM service principal.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: The signed-in user needs the AI Administrator role for these Agent-resource applyOnce operations.
claims.quote:
microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes | CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite | AI Administrator
microsoft.agent.useraccess | CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite | AI Administrator

claims.claim: Tenant Configuration Management remediation and applyOnce for these resources are preview capabilities through Graph beta.
claims.quote: Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) drift remediation and applyOnce monitors change workload configuration on behalf of the signed-in administrator. These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools.
In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP.
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The Policy tab, when available, lets an administrator turn general Work IQ MCP policy on or off tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.
Review the current policy state, then turn policy on or off for the tenant as needed.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy changes can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: No API operation for the Work IQ MCP tenant policy on/off setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy API settings tenant; Work IQ MCP policy PATCH. Read policy-governance-mcp, Package Management API overview and returned MCP reference excerpts; policy behavior and UI are documented, but no operation for this policy toggle was returned.

claims.claim: A separate Work IQ-specific administrator control for federated connectors is not documented on either surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated participation control Graph; Work IQ federated connectors default enable participation admin control. Read Work IQ overview and manage-federated-connectors; existing connector controls apply, but no separate Work IQ-specific connector admin switch or operation is given.

claims.claim: Users approve individual write tools in Copilot Chat, and Always allow and Allow for conversation apply per tool rather than per connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector. Users can decide which tools to allow.

claims.claim: Connector actions can be audited in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The instruction to review each connector's write tools has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: Review each connector's write tools. Table: connector availability; publisher-type access; User access; Work IQ MCP policy; missing Work IQ-specific connector control. No row covers reviewing connector tools.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Review each connector's write tools.' It names a control review with no corresponding table row.
